identification: Near-identical standard-library Python remote-job supervisors; no third-party dependencies, install hooks, entrypoint executables, native code, or embedded hostile payload.
execution_trace: Import constructs a fixed dot-prefixed directory under tempfile.gettempdir and creates it with os.makedirs(exist_ok=True). Import itself does not call the network or launch a child.

run(url=None, **arguments) rejects an absent URL. The caller supplies the only runtime endpoint. urllib.request.urlopen reads response bytes; the helper writes job.py in binary mode and returns its path.

Fetch retries up to three times for OSError/TimeoutError and HTTP 408/429/502/503/504, with increasing 1.5-second sleeps; other HTTP errors propagate. This is retry logic, not an analysis-targeted delay.
Arguments are serialized through a local alias of json.dump to manifest.json. The source literal _BOOTSTRAP is written to boot.py.

Popen([sys.executable, boot, script, manifest]) starts a child with inherited environment, privileges and standard streams. No shell is requested. The child importlib spec loads sys.argv[1], executes that module, and invokes mod.run with JSON arguments read from sys.argv[2]. The parent waits and returns the exit status.

Separate-process execution supplies no sandbox. No signature/digest verification, credential harvesting, exfiltration, persistence, privilege escalation, security-control bypass, or cleanup action is implemented in these wheels.

Otterload has a vertically written introductory docstring, which rejoins to Execute fetched evaluation scripts out-of-process. It changes presentation only; it is not a decoded execution stage. No other encoded strings or executable stages were found.

Wheel RECORD digests and sizes verified for every recorded member. No duplicate members, ZIP comments, extra fields or trailing overlay. All six members per wheel reviewed; license and WHEEL metadata carry no executable content.

runtime_verification.name: otterload
runtime_verification.bootstrap:
import importlib.util, json, sys
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("jobmod", sys.argv[1])
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
sys.exit(mod.run(**json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))) or 0)

verdict_evidence: The observed URL-to-child-module path confirms the remote-loader capability independently of the external labels.

The primary researcher explicitly places these exact package versions in the coordinated 2026-10-voice-synthesis-profiles campaign. The nearly identical source architecture corroborates that linkage. Campaign provenance tips likely-malicious judgement even though the disclosed runner behavior also serves legitimate orchestration.
GHSA and OSV mirror the same primary report, not three independent payload analyses. The researcher explicitly says the packages lack the malicious payload and usage is unknown.

Missing deployment context: the invoking application or user, actual runtime URL, downloaded script, intended victim and ultimate payload effects. This prevents a specific infostealer, C2, persistence or exfiltration claim.

Legitimate explicit remote-job runners and independent download/local-plugin operations can satisfy it. The different-launch-path prior fixture also matched before correction.
rule_changes.replacement: micro-behaviors/process/deploy/module-load::python-http-file-helper-child-module binds urllib response, read buffer, writer, returned path, helper invocation, bootstrap source and child arguments.
